model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on tangible book (engine route)

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY0 = FY2026E NET revenues (total revenues less interest expense, XBRL RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense), the line RJF reports and margins on. 9M-FY2026 actual 11,522 (Q1 3,735 / Q2 3,859 / Q3 3,928) plus a Q4 (Jul-Sep 2026, ended but not yet reported) estimate of ~4,020: fee-based PCG accounts bill on record 30-Jun client assets (~$1.92T AUA) and Clark Capital (consolidated from 1-May-2026) contributes a full quarter, partly offset by guided ~+1% sequential NII+RJBDP. 15,540 is +10.5% on FY2025's 14,065. DATA FLAG: the CSV/metrics 'Revenue' column is GROSS total revenues (FY2025 15,912), which includes ~$1.85B of interest expense that is netted out in net revenues; do not mix the two bases.
inputs.share_count_basis: Fully diluted: 10-Q cover-page common shares 192,361,711 (dei:EntityCommonStockSharesOutstanding as of 2026-08-03, filed 2026-08-05) plus 3.2M dilutive share-based awards (Q3-FY2026 WeightedAverageNumberDilutedSharesOutstandingAdjustment). Held FLAT because SBC is expensed inside compensation; buybacks (FY2025 $1.1B / 7.4M shares; 9M-FY2026 $1.2B / 7.7M shares) are how FCFE is distributed, not a modelled count reduction.
inputs.net_debt_note: Bank/broker convention (house precedent NAB.AX, HBAN, NTRS, GL): bank deposits ($63.3B at 30-Jun-2026), other borrowings ($950M FHLB) and the parent's senior notes ($3,522M, raised from $2,040M in FY2025) are funding whose interest cost is ALREADY deducted inside net revenues (interest expense is netted there), so pretax income is post-interest and the flow is FCFE. Net debt is therefore held at 0 and the flows are capitalised at the cost of equity; deducting the senior notes as well would charge their cost twice. The metrics CSV's NULL TotalDebt is NOT zero debt - it is simply irrelevant on this route. Symmetrically, the parent's surplus cash and the firm's capital above regulatory targets are NOT added (see valuation_philosophy).
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is the FY2026E FCFE proxy: net income ~2,282 (pretax 2,984 at a 19.2% margin on 15,540 net revenues, 23.5% tax) less 816 of capital retention at 0.5 x the 10.5% FY2026 growth (the base-case k). reported_fcf is the CSV's FY2025 OCF-less-capex (2,434 - 188); for a broker/bank it is deposit- and client-cash-flow noise (FY2023 -3,687, FY2024 +1,950, 9M-FY2026 swings from -56 to +1,054 by quarter) and is recorded for auditability only. The owner-FCF identity last_fcf = reported_fcf - sbc - interest_income deliberately does NOT hold on this route.
inputs.sbc_source: SEC XBRL ShareBasedCompensation (cash-flow add-back) FY2025 = $254M (1.81% of net revenues); 9M-FY2026 $183M (~1.6% annualised). No separate equity-award tax-withholding figure is tagged; it is treated as part of buyback cash. SBC is already inside compensation expense, so the pretax margin is post-SBC; sbc_pct_path is carried so the engine's house/street band is computed.
inputs.interest_income_note: Not stripped: net interest income ($2,147M FY2025) and RJBDP sweep fees are core operating revenue for a broker with a bank, not a return on surplus cash.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 StockRepurchasedDuringPeriodValue $1.1B + common dividends $416M = $1,516M returned vs $2,130M net income to common (71% payout). 9M-FY2026: buybacks $1.2B + dividends $326M = $1,526M vs $1,699M (90%), plus $484M cash for Clark Capital and $81M Series A preferred redemption - excess capital is being drawn down. Quarterly dividend $0.54 ($2.16 annualised, 1.4% yield). $1.1B of the $2.0B authorisation remained at 30-Jun-2026.
inputs.fy0_note: Fiscal year ends 30 September. FY2026 closed two days before the valuation date but is not yet reported (Q4 results due late October 2026), so FY0 is the FY2026E estimate (9M actual + Q4 estimate) and Y1 = FY2027. Last fully reported year is FY2025.
inputs.share_count_date: 2026-08-03 (10-Q cover page); dilutive awards from the quarter ended 2026-06-30

balance_sheet_anchors.goodwill_and_intangibles_note: Jumped from 1,838 (Dec-25) to 2,608 (Jun-26) on Clark Capital (~$305M goodwill, ~$330M intangibles) and smaller bolt-ons
balance_sheet_anchors.preferred_note: Series A preferred ($79M carrying) redeemed in Q2-FY2026 for $81M; PreferredStockValue = 0 at 31-Mar and 30-Jun-2026, so no preferred claim remains

inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 9.75% in USD: 10-yr UST ~4.25%, equity risk premium 5.0%, beta ~1.1 (RJF's earnings are levered to equity-market levels through fee-based AUA, to the Fed funds rate through NII/RJBDP, and to the M&A cycle through Capital Markets). Single rate across all three scenarios so risk is charged once, through the probability weights. Labelled 'wacc' only because that is the engine's field; no debt sits in the capital being discounted. Matches NTRS (same date, same build).
inputs.lease_treatment: Operating leases (branch/office premises) are expensed in occupancy & equipment inside non-interest expense and therefore inside the pretax margin; no lease liability is added to net debt and no separate lease line is carried (treatment A, applied once).
inputs.nci_treatment: Non-controlling interests $84M at 30-Jun-2026 (up from $1M at Sep-25, largely acquisition-related) are deducted at book in equity_bridge rather than charged in the flows; NCI share of net income is immaterial (<0.5%).
inputs.engine_mapping: The component engine is driven as a broker/bank P&L, identical to the NTRS/HBAN mapping: 'EBITDA margin' = pretax margin + D&A % + SBC %, so that EBITDA - SBC - D&A = pretax income (after interest expense, loan-loss provisions and all non-interest expense); cash_tax_rate turns that into net income; da_pct and capex_pct share a 1.35% core (FY2025 DepreciationAmortizationAndAccretionNet 195 = 1.39% vs capex 188 = 1.34% of net revenues, i.e. D&A ~= capex), and the EXCESS of capex_pct over da_pct is the capital retained to grow the bank balance sheet and fund bolt-on M&A - retention = k x revenue growth, k = 0.5 base / 0.4 bull / 0.65 bear. TCE/net revenue is ~0.65x, so k = 0.65 means all capital scales one-for-one with revenue; 0.5 reflects that ~70% of revenue is PCG/asset-management fees on client assets that consume little regulatory capital, while the bank segment's loan book and acquisitions do. Working-capital capture is 0. Resulting flow = FCFE = net income - retained capital, capitalised at the cost of equity.
inputs.notes: MODEL: Bank FCFE at cost of equity on tangible book, through the component engine route - the routing table's bank row implemented the way the house does it for HBAN, NTRS, NAB.AX and GL: net_debt = 0, senior claims (here NCI only) deducted in equity_bridge, capital retention tied to growth. RJF is a financial holding company whose largest business (PCG, ~73% of net revenue) is a capital-light wealth platform, but it owns Raymond James Bank ($63B deposits, Fed-regulated BHC), so OCF is dominated by client-cash and deposit flows and an owner-FCF DCF is meaningless (reported FCF -3,687 FY2023, +2,246 FY2025). BVPS-compounding was rejected because RJF distributes 70-90% of earnings and has been running down excess capital; book growth understates earnings power. FY0 ANCHOR: FY2026E net revenues 15,540, pretax margin 19.2% (9M actual 19.2%: 2,213 / 11,522; Q3 19.1%), tax 23.5% (9M actual 23.1%; FY2025 21.3% flattered by non-taxable corporate-owned life insurance gains), net income ~2,282, diluted EPS ~$11.67 on 195.6M shares - 13.7x the current price. GAAP not 'adjusted': adjusted EPS adds back acquisition costs and intangible amortisation (Q3 $3.14 vs $3.01 GAAP); bolt-on M&A is recurring for RJF so the house basis does not add it back. No notable one-offs in 9M-FY2026 large enough to strip (Clark deal costs ~$0.13/share in Q3). Prior judgments: none - first valuation of RJF.

equity_bridge.item: Non-controlling interests at book (30-Jun-2026 balance sheet)
equity_bridge.note: XBRL MinorityInterest 84; claim on consolidated flows not attributable to RJF common holders

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: base-case FY2027-FY2036 average net-revenue growth (7.0% tapering to 4.0%); the historical CAGRs are flattered by FY2020's COVID trough and by FY2022-24 rate hikes lifting NII/RJBDP from near zero, neither of which repeats with the Fed cutting
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity 5-yr CAGR 11.7% vs EPS 5-yr CAGR 21.6% - divergence >30%. Cause: the FY2020 base (EPS $3.96, COVID provisions + zero rates) is depressed, and buybacks cut the diluted count from 216.9M (FY2023) to ~196M; equity grows slower than EPS because 70-90% of earnings is distributed. Revenue 5-yr (12.0%) and equity 5-yr (11.7%) agree.
historical_growth.notes: Revenue CAGRs are on NET revenues (XBRL RevenuesNetOfInterestExpense: FY2025 14,065 / FY2022 11,003 / FY2020 7,990), not the CSV's gross total revenues. FCF CAGRs are computed on NET INCOME as the FCFE proxy (FY2025 2,135 / FY2022 1,509 / FY2020 818), not on the CSV's reported FCF, which is client-cash and deposit-flow noise. EPS diluted: 10.53 / 7.16 / 3.96 (split-adjusted for the Sep-2021 3:2 split). Equity per CSV: 12,504 / 9,432 / 7,176.

base.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin = EBITDA - SBC - D&A = [19.0, 19.3, 19.6, 19.9, 20.0, ...]: FY2027 dips ~20bps from FY0's 19.2% as the 125bps of cumulative Fed cuts keep compressing NII/RJBDP while fee revenue grows, then operating leverage on fee-based assets and Clark Capital integration lift it to management's long-standing 20% pretax-margin target by FY2031 and hold there.
base.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.5 x revenue growth = [3.5, 3.5, 3.25, 3.0, 3.0, 2.75, 2.5, 2.25, 2.0, 2.0]% of revenue: ~23% of net income retained in FY2027 (a ~77% payout, between FY2025's 71% and 9M-FY2026's 90%), falling to ~13% at the terminal year.
base.terminal_note: Cap 14x FCFE (~12x terminal net income) - the exit a buyer of a mature, fee-heavy wealth platform with a bank attached plausibly pays (RJF's 10-yr trailing P/E range roughly 10-17x). Gordon at 9.75%/3.0% is 15.3x, so the cap binds.

bull.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [20.0, 20.5, 21.0, 21.5, 22.0, ...]: recruiting momentum (multi-billion-dollar teams from Commonwealth, Stifel, Comerica) and a capital-markets M&A recovery lift fee revenue faster than the cost base; Clark Capital and AI-advisor productivity tools add operating leverage, taking RJF to an LPL/Morgan-Stanley-wealth-like 22%.
bull.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.4 x revenue growth: more of the growth is capital-light fee growth on client assets.
bull.terminal_note: Cap 15x FCFE; Gordon at 15.3x, so the cap binds marginally.

bear.pretax_margin_path_note: Implied pretax margin [16.7, 17.2, 17.7, 18.2, ...]: a ~25% equity bear market cuts fee-based billings (quarterly in advance on prior-quarter-end assets), the Fed cuts further and clients sort cash into money funds (NII+RJBDP down ~20%), capital markets falls back to the FY2023 trough, and loan provisions rise; RJF's sticky advisor payout and tech spend leave the margin near FY2023's 17-18%, recovering only to 18.2%.
bear.retention_note: capex_pct - da_pct = 0.65 x revenue growth (all capital scales one-for-one with revenue), floored at zero in FY2027 when revenue falls (no capital release assumed in a stress year).
bear.terminal_note: Cap 12x FCFE for a de-rated, slower-growing broker whose NII tailwind has fully reversed.

scenario_narratives.base: Raymond James' value turns on three things: (1) client assets under administration (~$1.92T at Jun-2026) compounding through market appreciation plus net new assets from the hybrid employee/independent recruiting model, which drives PCG and asset-management fees (~80% of net revenue); (2) net interest income and RJBDP sweep fees, which ballooned with the 2022-24 rate cycle and are now being compressed by 125bps of cuts and cash sorting - management guides only ~+1% sequential; (3) the pretax margin, which sits at 19.2% and which the base case lets reach management's 20% target by FY2031. Net revenues grow 7% in FY2027-28 (Clark Capital full-year, recruiting, market drift offset by NII drag), tapering to 4% by FY2035-36. About three-quarters of earnings is distributed via the $0.54 quarterly dividend and buybacks; the rest funds bank balance-sheet growth and bolt-on deals. Exit at 14x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bull: Recruiting accelerates (wirehouse breakaways and independent-channel consolidation keep sending multi-billion-dollar teams), markets compound, and the M&A/underwriting cycle recovers with lower rates, taking net revenue growth to ~10% in FY2027 and keeping it above 8% through FY2030. Operating leverage and AI-driven advisor productivity push the pretax margin to 22% by FY2031. Capital-light fee growth means only 0.4x growth is retained; exit at 15x FCFE.
scenario_narratives.bear: A ~25% equity drawdown in FY2027 hits asset-based fees immediately, further Fed cuts plus cash sorting cut NII/RJBDP by about a fifth, capital markets returns to trough, and credit provisions rise in the bank's CRE and corporate books: net revenue falls 6% and the pretax margin drops to ~16.7% on a sticky payout and technology cost base. Recovery is to 5% growth and an 18% margin, all growth requires proportional capital (0.65x), and the exit multiple de-rates to 12x FCFE.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: 25/50/25 rather than the 15/50/35 house default: RJF's earnings are explicitly exposed to two macro variables it cannot control (equity-market levels via fee-based AUA, and the Fed funds rate via NII/RJBDP, which management itself flags as the key swing factor), on top of a cyclical capital-markets segment. Symmetric weights match NTRS, valued the same day on the same rationale.

valuation_philosophy.summary: RJF is valued as distributable equity cash flow - net income less the capital needed to grow the bank balance sheet and buy bolt-ons - discounted at a 9.75% USD cost of equity, with no net-debt deduction because every funding cost (deposits, FHLB, senior notes) is already inside net revenues. The engine's 'EBITDA', 'D&A' and 'capex' fields are a mapping device: EBITDA - SBC - D&A = pretax income, and capex in excess of D&A = retained capital. The valuation deliberately does not add the capital RJF holds above its regulatory targets or the parent's surplus cash, which is conservative by roughly $1-2B (~$5-10/share); it also does not add back acquired-intangible amortisation, which management's 'adjusted' EPS does.
key_risks_to_valuation: Rate path: NII + RJBDP fees are a large share of pretax income; each further 25bp Fed cut compresses them, and cash sorting into money funds shrinks the sweep base itself
Market levels: fee-based PCG and asset-management revenue bill on client assets, so a 20-25% equity drawdown flows through to revenue within one to two quarters (the bear case)
Capital-markets cyclicality: M&A advisory and underwriting can swing segment pretax income by several hundred million dollars year to year
Recruiting economics: forgivable loans and transition packages for recruited teams are capital-intensive; if recruited assets underperform the k=0.5 retention assumption is too low
Credit: the bank's CRE, corporate and SBL loan books are the source of loss risk in a recession; FY2023 provisions were $292M
Exit multiple: 14x FCFE (~12x terminal net income) in the base; RJF's own trailing P/E has ranged ~10-17x, so the terminal value is sensitive to where in that range the market prices a mature RJF
